text:
#Forex #GBPUSD UPDATE – The Week Ahead
Commencing Monday 16 November 2026

Spot GBP/USD: 1.3213 / 1.3215

(Friday 13 November close near 1.3213. Day’s range about 1.3204-1.3253. The pair has given back the mid-week gains above 1.3450 and finished the week lower. Market closed.)

1. Macro and Political Drivers

Cable closed the week near 1.3213 after a hot US CPI print on Tuesday and a lack of sustained follow-through from the Bank of England’s hawkish hike the previous week. The pair tested as high as 1.3460 early in the week before the inflation data and subsequent dollar strength reversed the move. The policy gap remains dollar-favourable at the margin, even after Bank Rate was raised to 4% on 5 November.

Three themes now govern the week ahead.

(a) A firm US inflation print. October CPI rose 0.4% month-on-month against a consensus near 0.3%, with core CPI up 0.3% against an expected 0.2%. It was the third consecutive month of gains of 0.4% or more on the headline. The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not publish year-on-year figures because of last year’s government shutdown. The print reinforces residual December Federal Reserve hike pricing after the October hold at 3.75%-4.00%. Strong labour data the previous Friday (payrolls +165,000, unemployment 4.1%) had already kept that path open; the CPI result makes a further move more difficult to dismiss.

b) A heavy UK data week. Tuesday brings the labour market report (unemployment, employment change, average earnings). Wednesday is the October CPI print. Friday brings retail sales. These three releases will decide whether the Bank of England’s 8-1 vote to hike to 4%, and the projection of inflation approaching 5% in mid-2027, remains the base case into December. A firm CPI or sticky wages would support further tightening bets and offer sterling some relief. A soft print would reopen downside toward the recent lows.

(c) Oil’s continued correction. Front-month WTI closed Friday near $88.56 and Brent near $95.84. Both contracts have fallen sharply from the levels above $100-$110 seen in late October. Lower oil is marginally helpful for UK real incomes and reduces one source of imported inflation pressure, but it also removes residual support for the dollar’s energy-linked bid. The net effect on cable remains two-way: less inflation pressure supports the Bank of England’s ability to stay restrictive without crushing growth, while a softer oil price can reduce safe-haven dollar demand.
The week is lighter on policy decisions but heavy on data. Tuesday’s US retail sales and Wednesday’s FOMC minutes will be watched for any further guidance on the December path. Fed speakers are scattered throughout. There is no Bank of England decision until December.

Full Economic Calendar – Key Events for GBPUSD (16-20 November 2026)

Monday 16 November

US Empire State Manufacturing Index (November) - medium impact.
Canada CPI (October) - high impact, external.
China activity data (October) - medium impact, external.
Fed speakers (Williams, Warsh, Barr).
Thin UK calendar. ASEAN Summit begins.

Tuesday 17 November

UK labour market (October / three months to September) - high impact. Unemployment rate, employment change, average earnings. Previous unemployment around 4.7%. 07:00 London.
US retail sales advance (October) - high impact. Consensus about +0.2% month-on-month (previous +0.8%). 13:30 London.
US industrial production and capacity utilisation (October) - medium impact.
US import/export prices - medium impact.
Fed speakers.
Eurozone and German ZEW - external.

Wednesday 18 November

UK CPI, core CPI and PPI (October) - high impact. 07:00 London. The single most important UK print of the week.
FOMC minutes (October meeting) - high impact. 19:00 London. Watch for any detail on the two dissents and the path toward a further hike.
US housing starts and building permits (October) - medium impact.
US pending home sales - medium impact.
Eurozone CPI final - external.
Bank of England speaker (Pill).

Thursday 19 November

US initial jobless claims - medium impact.
US Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Index (November) - medium impact.
Fed speakers (Hammack, Goolsbee, Paulson, Kashkari).
Australian employment - external.
Japan CPI - external.

Friday 20 November

UK retail sales (October) - high impact. 07:00 London.
US University of Michigan consumer sentiment, final (November) - medium impact.
Canada retail sales - external.
China LPR - external.

Overall: this is a UK inflation and labour week with US retail sales and FOMC minutes as the main dollar-side catalysts. A firm UK CPI would support the Bank of England’s tightening bias and allow a squeeze toward 1.3300-1.3350. Soft UK data plus firm US retail sales would pressure cable toward 1.3150-1.3136. The broader backdrop remains dollar-supported after the hot CPI, though the Bank of England’s hike has narrowed the policy gap at the margin.

2. DXY and Yield Correlation

The dollar index has held near the upper end of its recent range after the CPI beat. Two-year US yields should stay supported by residual December hike pricing. Two-year gilt yields have risen on the Bank of England hike and the inflation projection near 5%, but the differential remains dollar-favourable unless UK CPI is materially hotter than expected. Sterling rallies that are not backed by firm UK inflation data tend to be sold.

3. Options and Gamma Structure

At 1.3213, cable has broken back below the mid-1.33s. Upside gamma now sits into 1.3280-1.3320, with a secondary concentration near 1.3350-1.3420. Downside magnets have shifted to 1.3150 and the recent swing low area around 1.3136. Into Wednesday’s UK CPI, hedging flows argue for selling a test of 1.3280-1.3320 rather than buying the bounce from 1.3213.

4. Liquidity and Order Flow Map

Buy-side liquidity sits above 1.3280-1.3320, then 1.3350-1.3420. Sell-side pools sit below 1.3150 and 1.3136. The rejection from 1.3460 left residual stops above 1.3350. The higher-probability flow this week is to sell strength into the UK data rather than chase the Friday close.

5. Sentiment – Last 24 Hours

Weekend commentary is subdued after the CPI-driven dollar rally. The dominant read is that the Bank of England’s hike was necessary but not sufficient to offset firm US inflation and a still-resilient labour market. Positioning appears light ahead of Wednesday’s UK CPI, with most desks reluctant to add size before the print.

6. Technical Structure

Cable tested 1.3507 earlier in the month, rejected the 1.3460 area, and closed Friday at 1.3213. The move remains a corrective bounce inside a broader downtrend until 1.3420 is reclaimed on a daily close. The 200-day average continues to sit in the 1.3430 area and remains well above current price.
Key Levels for the Week:

Resistance: 1.3280-1.3320 (near-term sell zone), then 1.3350-1.3420
Support: 1.3150 (near-term), 1.3136 (recent swing low area), then 1.3100

Daily structure stays bearish below 1.3350.

7. Week-Ahead Scenario Model and Bias

Primary scenario (60% probability): A bounce into 1.3280-1.3320 early in the week or on firm UK data, then selling if CPI undershoots or retail sales disappoint. Follow-through toward 1.3150, extending to 1.3136.

Secondary scenario (40% probability): A firm UK CPI combined with soft US retail sales squeezes the pair through 1.3320 toward 1.3350-1.3420. That would force a reassessment of the near-term bearish bias.

Definitive Week-Ahead Trade Suggestion

Bias: Preferentially bearish - sell rallies. Do not chase shorts from 1.3213 into Monday’s open.

Trade: Sell GBP/USD on rallies toward 1.3280-1.3320.
 Stop Loss: 1.3365 (risk about 45-85 points depending on entry).

 Take Profit: First target 1.3150, extension 1.3100 (reward about 130-220 points from the sell zone).

From a mid-zone entry near 1.3300, risk to 1.3365 is 65 points against 150-200 points of downside. Prefer the upper end of the zone (closer to 1.3320) if Monday or Tuesday is already bid, to keep the ratio nearer 1:2.

Invalidation: A sustained daily close above 1.3365 would cancel the sell-the-rally plan and force a reassessment toward 1.3420.

Conclusion

The week commencing 16 November 2026 is a UK CPI and labour week. Cable closed Friday at 1.3213 after a hot US CPI print of +0.4% month-on-month. Oil has corrected further to around $89 and $96. The dollar remains supported by residual December hike pricing. Sterling rallies into 1.3280-1.3320 remain selling opportunities unless Wednesday’s UK CPI is materially firmer than expected.

Disclaimer

My analysis is for discussion and informational purposes only. Foreign exchange trading involves substantial risk and may not be suitable for all investors. Risk management and position sizing must always be considered carefully. I am a professional former interbank currency trader now trading privately, and any views expressed represent my own trading opinions and personal trading activity and are not investment advice or suitable for all market participants.

Glen Taylor bought the entire Minnesota Timberwolves for $88.5 million in 1994. Three years later he gave one 21-year-old $126 million.

1995: Kevin Garnett goes straight from high school to the NBA. First player in 20 years to do it.

Summer 1997: Minnesota offers him about $103 million over six years. He says no. The owner makes the rejection public, and everyone calls a 20-year-old greedy.

Oct 1, 1997, one hour before the deadline: six years, $126 million. The biggest contract in team sports history.

The rest of the league lost it. Owners locked the players out in 1998 and wiped out half a season. The deal that ended it created the NBA's first max salary. Contracts like KG's were banned.

Then it got worse for Minnesota. The league caught them in a secret side deal with another player and took away three first-round picks. Huge money in one player, no picks to build around him.

KG retired with more than $330 million in career earnings, the most in NBA history. Taylor sold the team for $1.5 billion.

The case for KG: he bet on himself at 20 and won by $23 million.

The case for Taylor: he paid so much the whole league changed the rules, and his own team paid for it for a decade.

Crypto has seen this movie: one wild deal, then the rules show up. Who was right?

text:
Salvation Army (2013) – Morocco 🇲🇦 🏳️‍🌈

A deeply moving and intimate queer drama about growing up gay in a conservative Moroccan Muslim society, where desire, family expectations, social class and personal freedom often collide.

The film follows Abdellah, a young boy growing up in Casablanca, who begins discovering his s3xu@lity and developing an attraction to older men. As he grows older, his journey takes him beyond Morocco, where he continues searching for love, independence and a place where he can truly be himself.

Based on the autobiographical novel by Moroccan writer and filmmaker Abdellah Taïa, the film draws from deeply personal experiences of growing up gay in a society where homosxuality is heavily stigmatized.

What makes this film worth watching?

 Its honest portrayal of gay identity and self discovery in a conservative environment.

 The complicated relationship between desire, loneliness, intimacy and the need for affection.

 Its exploration of forbidden attraction, secrecy and the emotional challenges of growing up different.

🎬 Its intimate storytelling, understated performances and realistic depiction of everyday life in Morocco.

Unlike conventional romance films, Salvation Army doesn't rely on dramatic love stories or happy endings. It offers a raw, sometimes uncomfortable and deeply human portrait of a young man trying to understand himself and find his place in the world.

A must-watch for anyone interested in international queer cinema and stories that explore the realities of being gay in Muslim societies.

A gay Muslim teenager struggles with his growing feelings for his English teacher while facing family expectations and an arranged marriage to a woman.

Three young Muslims living in Berlin experience personal crises that challenge their faith, beliefs, sexuality and understanding of love. One storyline explores the feelings between two young men.

A heartfelt short film about a queer Muslim Arab boy discovering his identity and finding support in his older brother, who encourages him to embrace who he is.

Two closeted Muslim teenagers living in Brooklyn secretly navigate their romantic relationship while dealing with family expectations, FBI surveillance, racial profiling and their sxuality.

text:
Nehemiah 4
 
New International Version
Opposition to the Rebuilding
4 [a]When Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he became angry and was greatly incensed. He ridiculed the Jews, 2 and in the presence of his associates and the army of Samaria, he said, “What are those feeble Jews doing? Will they restore their wall? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they finish in a day? Can they bring the stones back to life from those heaps of rubble—burned as they are?”

3 Tobiah the Ammonite, who was at his side, said, “What they are building—even a fox climbing up on it would break down their wall of stones!”

text:
In the winter of 1944, Gena Turgel was pushed naked into a freezing concrete room at Auschwitz-Birkenau with hundreds of other women. The heavy iron doors slammed shut behind them. Everyone knew what was supposed to happen next.💔

Gena had already lost almost everything. Most of her family had been swallowed by the horror of the Krakow ghetto and the camps. One brother was shot by the SS. Another vanished after escaping. A sister and her husband were executed for trying to smuggle food. Now, standing shoulder to shoulder with terrified women in that cold room, she believed her own life had finally reached its last few minutes.

Some women cried quietly. Some prayed. Others simply stared ahead, too exhausted even to be afraid anymore. Gena waited for the Zyklon B gas to come through the pipes. She waited to stop breathing.

But nothing happened. One minute passed. Then another. The room stayed silent. The gas never came. Whether it was a mechanical failure, a mistake, or something no one could ever fully explain, the valves remained closed. Then suddenly, the doors opened again. The guards stared in disbelief. The women were still alive. And Gena walked out.

Years later, she would describe that moment with only a few words: “God must have protected me.”

But surviving that room did not mean the nightmare was over. Gena was later forced onto a death march and eventually sent to Bergen-Belsen, where hunger, disease and death were everywhere. Bodies lay in heaps around the camp. People disappeared by the hour. Hope itself seemed to be dying. She worked in the camp hospital, trying to keep her mother alive and offering what little care she could to the dying.

And there, among thousands of suffering prisoners, Gena encountered a desperately sick teenage girl. Her name was Anne Frank. By then, Anne was no longer the bright young girl who had once filled the pages of her diary with dreams. She was feverish, weak and terribly thin. Typhus was destroying what little strength remained in her body.

Gena remembered trying to care for her. She brought Anne water. She tried to wash her. She stayed close when fear and fever overwhelmed her. In a place built to erase compassion, Gena offered the one thing the Nazis had not managed to destroy completely: human kindness. Anne was frightened and delirious, but Gena never forgot the softness that still remained in her. She would remember her eyes for the rest of her life. Eyes that belonged to a child who should have been thinking about school, friendship and the future… not death.

Anne never made it out of Bergen-Belsen. Gena did.

Then came April 15, 1945. British troops entered the camp. For Gena, liberation did not feel like a celebration at first. She was alive, but she carried the dead with her. Her family. The women from the camps. The children. Anne. And yet, among the ruins of one of humanity’s darkest chapters, something extraordinary happened.

Gena met Norman Turgel, a British soldier. She was painfully thin. Her body had been weakened by years of starvation and suffering. But Norman saw something the camps had failed to take from her. Life. Strength. Dignity. And somehow, in a place surrounded by death, love began.

Only months after liberation, Gena and Norman were married. Her wedding dress was made from the silk of a British Army parachute. It was more than a dress. It was a symbol. Fabric once meant to carry men safely from the sky was now wrapped around a woman who had somehow fallen through the darkest depths of history and survived. Not long before, Gena had stood naked behind locked doors, waiting to die. Now she stood dressed as a bride, preparing to live.

That wedding dress would later be preserved at the Imperial War Museum in London. But Gena’s greatest legacy was never a dress. It was her voice.

She lived to the age of 95 and spent decades speaking to children and adults about what she had witnessed. She could have allowed hatred to consume the rest of her life. Instead, she chose remembrance. She chose family. She chose love. And she chose to speak for those who never had the chance to grow old.

Gena Turgel survived ghettos, concentration camps, starvation, disease and a room she believed would become her grave. But perhaps the most powerful part of her story is what happened afterward. The Nazis tried to teach her that human life meant nothing. Gena spent the rest of hers proving the opposite.

She walked into Auschwitz as a terrified young woman expecting death. She walked out of history as a wife, a mother, a grandmother, a survivor—and a voice for millions who never came home.

Sometimes hope does not arrive loudly. Sometimes it is simply one more breath… when you were certain there would be no next one.

text:
In 280 BC, a blind old man was carried through the Forum on a litter.

Rome was losing a war. King Pyrrhus of Epirus, a kinsman of Alexander the Great, had come to Italy at the request of the Greek city of Tarentum, and at Heraclea he had crushed the Roman army. His own losses were heavy, though. So he sent his envoy Cineas to the Senate with an offer of peace. Rome only had to leave the Greek cities of southern Italy alone.

Many senators were ready to accept.

That was until Appius Claudius Caecus, a veteran of Rome’s earlier wars, was brought into the Senate house to remind them what Rome was built on.

Had it not been for Caecus, Rome might have begun to decline before it even became a major power.

Today, we will discuss why it is important to remember the foundations of any civilization, empire, company or even family. Why relaxed standards cause a permanent rot that destroys everything from within, and how to protect yourself from it.

• One U.S. Army battalion offered eligible soldiers a four-day pass tied to reenlistment.

💰 HOW COULD THIS AFFECT THE ECONOMY?

• Staffing gaps could delay work and increase overtime costs.
• Game sales could boost Take-Two $TTWO.
• Console and accessory purchases could benefit the wider gaming industry.
• Other entertainment businesses could lose spending as players stay home.

The viral “$1 BILLION economic loss” figure is an estimate—not a confirmed hit to GDP.

Paid leave can shift when people work, and gaming purchases can shift where people spend. Neither automatically means the economy loses that entire amount.

For investors, the bigger story is how much launch excitement becomes sustained revenue and profit for $TTWO. 📈

🚨 BREAKING: Death Toll Rises to Five After Fire at Canadian Army Base Wainwright 🇨🇦🔥🎖️💔

A fifth Canadian soldier has died from injuries suffered in a fire during training at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta.
The Canadian Armed Forces named him as Private William Douglas Dal Bianco of the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry.
He died on November 13 while receiving medical care in Ontario, almost four weeks after the October 17 incident.
The military confirmed his death in an official statement from Ottawa on November 14.
According to the Armed Forces, 24 service members are still in hospital receiving treatment, while 14 others have been released.
Defence Minister David McGuinty offered his deepest condolences to the soldier's family, friends and comrades.
He said the government would keep supporting the families and the wider military community through this painful period.
Chief of the Defence Staff General Jennie Carignan said the whole Canadian Armed Forces was heartbroken by the loss.

text:
paused subscribers come back 54% of the time. a "please stay" discount at the cancel button keeps 22% (churnkey data across hundreds of cancel flows)

and apple just put retention offers inside the iOS cancel screen (nov 4). the cancel page is the most under-built screen in most products

> why people actually cancel
- churnkey, ~3M cancel sessions: budget 33%, infrequent usage 31%. their read: "budget" often hides product frustration
- prosperstack, jan-oct 2026: pricing 32%, no time 11%, temporary or seasonal 10%, couldn't build a habit 9%
- under 1% of those answers named an AI tool. ask it as its own option or it hides under "pricing"
- recurly: 51% of consumers who canceled said they weren't using it enough. 38% say they'd rather pause

> what each save is worth (churnkey)
- discount: +5.1 months. 11% still paying a year later
- pause: +5.5 months, picked 15 seconds faster than a discount
- plan change: +7-8 months. 30% still active at 12 months
- recurly: when pause is offered, 25% pick it over canceling

> the order that works
- one question first: why are you leaving
- "busy" / "not using it" -> pause. default 1 month, let them extend
- "too expensive" -> downgrade, then a small one-time discount
- pause goes before any discount. cap repeat pauses
- seat removals -> offer a handoff. superhuman cut seat removals 15% this way

> your save rate is probably fake
- retainup audited 8 subscription brands in 2026: median save 10.8%, best 19.3%
- one app dashboard said 62.5%. remove people who just closed the tab: 12.5%
- https://t.co/9ZZcvk02Jo math: 30% take the discount, 40% of them leave when it expires = ~18% real save
- https://t.co/9ZZcvk02Jo test, meditation app: reason-matched flow vs blanket 60% off = ~1.5x acceptance, ~4.5x LTV per save
- count a save once the next invoice pays

> setup
- stripe portal: retention coupon ships OFF. settings > customer portal > cancellations
- stripe retention rules: offer by cancel reason, months subscribed, total spend. one retention coupon per customer. their example: "too expensive" + 6+ months = 30% off for 3 months
- stripe pause: pause_collection + resumes_at. pick void or mark_uncollectible. keep_as_draft leaves invoices you can collect for the paused months later
- apple: retention messages in app store connect (text, image, switch plan, promo offer), shown after "cancel subscription". real-time API by request, answer in 700ms or apple shows your default

> the legal line
- california since jul 2025: save offers are fine online only with a "click to cancel" button shown next to the offer the whole time
- amazon's "iliad" flow: 4 pages, 6 clicks, 15 options vs 1-2 clicks to join. the case ended in a $2.5B ftc settlement
- ftc says uber one took up to 23 screens and 32 actions to cancel. uber disputes it
- federal click-to-cancel rule got vacated in 2025, ftc restarted it march 2026. ~30 states have their own laws

> the fight
one side: save offers pay your most annoyed customers to stay, and deal hunters learn to hit cancel every quarter
other side: no flow means someone who wanted a month off has to fire you
my take: one screen, reason first, one matched offer, cancel button visible the whole time. if it takes 4 screens to keep someone, you kept a hostage

> run this week
- export 90 days of cancel reasons. if budget wins, read the free text
- add pause as the first offer
- recount your save rate with next-invoice-paid only

bookmark this before you touch your cancel button

Against that backdrop, U.S. Representative Carlos Giménez of Florida sent Musk a formal letter dated November 9. The former Miami-Dade mayor urged Tesla to consider moving its headquarters from Austin to Florida or expanding operations there. He pointed to the election of self-described Democratic Socialists and warned of excessive government interference, politically motivated investigations, and policies that punish success. Florida, he wrote, offers lower taxes, responsible regulation, and an environment that rewards rather than targets job creators and innovators. South Florida’s infrastructure, skilled workforce, and position as a gateway to Latin America and the Caribbean were highlighted as practical advantages.

Outgoing Governor Ron DeSantis has already floated the idea of a Tesla gigafactory in the state. Florida itself resisted the national Democratic wave: Republican Byron Donalds defeated Democrat David Jolly to become the state’s first Black governor, preserving nearly three decades of uninterrupted GOP control of the executive branch. Donalds takes office in January 2027 with a mandate to continue the pro-business posture that has defined Florida under DeSantis.

Musk previously relocated Tesla’s headquarters from California to Texas in 2021, citing regulatory hostility. The same dynamic is now reappearing in Texas. Governor-elect Hinojosa has already intervened to pause discussions of selling portions of Boca Chica State Park land adjacent to SpaceX’s Starbase facility, stating that any relationship with Musk’s companies must occur “on our terms.” She has also signaled tighter scrutiny of large-scale data-center projects. Musk has publicly noted that Tesla and SpaceX thrived in Texas precisely because they avoided what he described as an oppressive and extractive state government.

The contrast is straightforward. Texas’s new Democratic leadership is signaling greater intervention in land use, permitting, and private investment. Florida’s incoming Republican administration is explicitly advertising the opposite: a jurisdiction that treats capital formation and technological deployment as assets rather than liabilities. Whether Musk acts on the invitation remains open, but the invitation itself underscores a clear sorting mechanism. States that prioritize regulatory restraint continue to compete for the companies and individuals that generate employment and technological advance, while those that do not risk watching them depart. https://t.co/3a6N059Tga

< Be Brian Lee
< Born 1971, Orange County, California
< Son of Korean immigrants who ran a wig shop
< You watch your parents work sixteen hour days for margins thinner than paper
< USC undergrad, then Georgetown Law
< Class of 1995, firm offers in hand
< You last eighteen months at a big firm before the exit
< Entertainment law seems like the move
< You end up repping small brands, learning how deals actually close
< 2007: you meet a shoe designer with a warehouse full of inventory
< Her name is Jessica Simpson
< You don't just do her contracts, you build the business
< $1 billion in retail sales within five years
< The legal work was the least interesting part
< You wanted to build things, not paper them
< 2009: you cold call a guy running an eyewear startup
< His name is Dave Gilboa, company is Warby Parker
< He doesn't need a lawyer. He needs operational help.
< You become employee number three
< The insight lands: direct to consumer brands need builders, not advisors
< 2011: you co-found LegalZoom with three partners
< The bet is simple. Most legal work is forms, not judgment.
< Lawyers charge $300 an hour to fill in blanks
< You charge $79
< The ABA calls it unauthorized practice of law
< Twenty state bars open investigations
< You call it democratization. They call it war.
< The company survives every challenge
< 2020: LegalZoom has served four million small businesses
< 2021: IPO at $7 billion valuation
< You were right about the forms. You were wrong about the moat.
< Competitors flood the market. Margins compress.
< The stock drops 80% from its peak
< You're already gone, building the next thing

The son of wig shop owners bet that law was mostly paperwork, and twenty state bars tried to prove him wrong.

They failed, then the market did what regulators couldn't.

He made legal services cheap, just not defensible.

text:
I've been a Christian now since 1979. Forty-seven years. From the very beginning God has had His loving hand upon me and my life. Trial after trial God has sent to me. God hasn't stopped sending me trials. He has allowed every one of them. The trials have never been light, but intense. Through all the pain. Through all the suffering, I have come to learn that God uses only one tool to build character in me. The tool of adversity. I have learned that God is in control of every aspect of my life. I have learned that nothing can come to me except what God allows. And what my God allows, in His Good Book, the Holy Bible, is "working together for my good." I have learned that the Holy Spirit that dwells in me is changing me from the inside. That I can't change myself on my own. That I will become more like my Master and Savior, Jesus Christ.

Ten years ago, God allowed me to become a widow. This is the biggest trial I have ever gone through. From my own husband's lips, shortly before he passed, he revealed to me that he was a great pretender. Pretending to still be a Christian after he walked away from God three years into our 35-year marriage. I was shattered. My heart was broken. It took me these past ten years to forgive him with God's forgiveness. I knew I didn't have the forgiveness in and of myself but knew only God's forgiveness could make it so. Finally, after vacillating back and forth of forgiving him with God's forgiveness, with the Holy Spirit gently convicting me, and with God's great love for me and His mercy and His grace moving my heart to do what is right according to the Word of God, I told God I truly, once and for all want to forgive me husband as You have forgiven me of all my sins against You. That would You please give me Your forgiveness for my husband. That is the desire of my heart. That was a couple months ago. To this day, I no longer have any ounce of hatred or bitterness towards my late husband. Only God's agape love and His forgiveness overflows within my heart which is finally cemented and sealed. Through God's great power, whenever the thought comes up of what he did to me, my heart and my mind and soul are overflowed with God's great love for him and God's forgiveness. That's what's there now. That's what God continues to do for me. An absolute miracle from God. Like only He can do.

These past ten years I've had to learn to trust in my God like never before. God has brought such fearful trials to me. Out of His great love for me He has brought them to me. For, I've come to learn, that God's trials have no bounds. Just because I am a widow, does not mean necessarily that my trials will not become any easier. His trials, according to His Word, are only "for my good." God's purpose in my trials is for me to grow more into the image of Christ.

In the Book of John 6:66-69, Jesus finished with some hard sayings to His disciples. Many said, "This is a hard saying, who can understand it?" From that time, many of His disciples went back and walked with Him no more. Then Jesus turned to the twelve apostles asking, "Do you also want to turn away?" Peter replied, "Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the Words of eternal life!" They didn't really understand everything Jesus was saying. It sounded pretty weird to them. But they had committed to Him and knew of no better options.

I previously lived on a three-acre beautiful cabin-style home in the country/forest since 2001 when God called me and my late husband to move from our beautiful home in Southern California near the Pacific Ocean to the Pacific Northwest. Our home was on a well. Five years after my husband passed, suddenly there was no water coming out of my faucets. Scared, I called out to God for His help. I lived fifteen miles from town. God led me to a plumber who had experience in wells. I needed a new well pump. Got me up and running. Two weeks later, I had no water. He said somewhere there is a leak which is slowly draining my well! How would he find the leak on my vast acreage? It looked impossible! I prayed to my God. I prayed for a miracle. I desperately needed a miracle. I knew in my heart of hearts that there is nothing impossible for God. Miraculously, he found the leak. One of my outdoor water spickets near my home had a tiny leak. 

Then last year, my 1994 Olds Bravada, that I absolutely love, was having turnover problems suddenly. I needed a mechanic close by within walking distance to leave my car to be worked on for two weeks. I needed a new rebuilt engine and a new exhaust system. God had led me to this place near the mall. I felt in my heart of hearts that God was going to make my vehicle great. That it was going to run better than ever with all these upgraded changes. I was excited. Most of the changes were great. But I still was having turnover problems! The manager said I need a new spider fuel injector, but they don't make them anymore! He said he had found one on ebay at the time of ordering my new rebuilt engine. But shortly after he ordered my engine, he found the fuel injector on ebay wasn't the right make for my Bravada! So, the manager never stopped the order of a new rebuilt engine. He knew about the fuel injector problem but didn't call and tell me. He said his mechanics could rebuild my fuel injector. I told him I would think about it. Once again, I had to trust my God. I no longer trusted this manager nor the mechanics. What was I to do? They were the only auto mechanics near me within walking distance. Once again, I had to go back to God's Word, "that all things work together for my good. That nothing can come to me except God allows." To this day, God has not had me have those mechanics rebuild my fuel injector. God has not had me go to the company, to the owner and tell him the cheating and deceit from the manager of hiding the fact of my fuel injector. What God has done for me is give to me many of His miracles. God has touched my fuel injector. It always starts. It always turns over. As for the other concerns from the mechanics working on my vehicle, every one of them, God has slowly but surely miraculously touched this past year. No longer are they problems from the mechanics that needed fixing. 

In the winter season right before New Years of 2026, my heating system in my mobile home suddenly stopped working. The weather was wintry. A cold snap. I ordered two portable heaters from Home Depot. I had to wait for a week for them to arrive. In the meantime, I had no heat. The week was right before New Years. By the time my heaters arrived, my indoor thermostat was at 47 degrees. God miraculously kept me warm with my down comforters and winter clothing. These are just a few recent trials God brought to me "for my good." In all of them, God held me close in His loving arms. Yes, I was scared. I was full of anxiety in each situation. But as I cried out to my God for His help, He never failed me. He always delivered me from all my fears. Depression. The blues. Discouragement. He held me close to Him. Never let me go. Never forsook me. And most importantly, He gave me what I needed to "not walk away" from Him in each of these trials. And to this day, I can truly testify...that my God is real. His Word is His TRUTH to me. His promises He always delivers.

The trials keep on coming. For my sake. Out of God's great love for me. Jesus is the author and finisher of my faith. "Being confident of this very thing, that He who has begun a good work in me will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ (Philippians 1:6) (who comes to take us home to be with Him forever - the Rapture (1 Thessalonians 4:16-17). In these trials, I am learning obedience to my Lord Jesus Christ. To "reckon the 'old Jennifer dead with Christ' (Romans 6:11). That I am a new creation in Christ. That I have a new nature. The nature of Christ (2 Corinthians 5:17). I no longer live, but Christ now lives in me (Galatians 2:20). Finally, throughout the trial, I am learning to pray, "Jesus, not my will, but Yours be done." In all of this, this is the life of "walking in the Spirit." The Christ-centered life. I can truly testify that I no longer am the same person I was forty-seven years ago. Mixed up. Heading for hell and didn't even know it. Thank God Jesus came and rescued me from Satan, my master. God has changed me so much. I have fallen so much in love with Jesus Christ. He is become the beat of my heart, my lifeline, my life. Where would I go? He holds the keys to eternal life. He's caused me to hunger and thirst for more of Him and His Word. With God's help. With God's grace, I keep running to Him. Never looking back to what used to be. The old Jennifer. The old desires. But looking at what is now. The new Jennifer. Filled with the Holy Spirit. Christ-centered. Who can't imagine living without Jesus as my Savior and as my Lord. 

I don't understand all what God is doing to me and for me. I get scared. I have no one to turn to but to God. God has planned it so. I have problems and difficulties. But where else can I go? I have already learned that the world has nothing to offer me. It can't solve my problems. There is really nothing to go back to. I have come to know, after walking forty-seven years with Jesus as my Savior and my Lord, that Jesus IS the only ANSWER. That all what He has allowed in my life, He has never let me go. He has never given up on me. He and His promises are real and are TRUE. So...I trust the One who has the Words of eternal life. And I can say with great love from my heart to my God, "You are the only true and living God. The eternal God. The Alpha and the Omega. The Beginning and the End. There is none like You and there never will be. I love you Father. I love You Jesus. I love you Holy Spirit. Thank you for never letting me go. You are Faithful and True." 🙏✝️✝️✝️

text:
The explosion in text-to-image AI models like OpenAI’s DALL-E 2—programs trained to generate pictures of almost anything you ask for—has sent ripples through the creative industries, from fashion to filmmaking, by providing weird and wonderful images on demand.

The same technology behind these programs is also making a splash in biotech labs, which have started using this type of generative AI, known as a diffusion model, to conjure up designs for new types of protein never seen in nature.

Today, two labs separately announced programs that use diffusion models to generate designs for novel proteins with more precision than ever before. Generate Biomedicines, a Boston-based startup, revealed a program called Chroma, which the company describes as the “DALL-E 2 of biology.”

At the same time, a team at the University of Washington led by biologist David Baker has built a similar program called RoseTTAFold Diffusion. In a preprint paper posted online today, Baker and his colleagues show that their model can generate precise designs for novel proteins that can then be brought to life in the lab. “We’re generating proteins with really no similarity to existing ones,” says Joe Watson, one of the co-developers of RoseTTAFold Diffusion.

These protein generators can be directed to produce designs for proteins with specific properties, such as shape or size or function. In effect, this makes it possible to come up with new proteins to do particular jobs on demand. Researchers hope that this will eventually lead to the development of new and more effective drugs. “We can discover in minutes what took evolution millions of years,” says Gevorg Grigoryan, CTO of Generate Biomedicines.

“What is notable about this work is the generation of proteins according to desired constraints,” says Ava Amini, a biophysicist at Microsoft Research in Cambridge, Massachusetts. 

Proteins are the fundamental building blocks of living systems. In animals, they digest food, contract muscles, detect light, drive the immune system, and so much more. When people get sick, proteins play a part. 

Proteins are thus prime targets for drugs. And many of today’s newest drugs are protein based themselves. “Nature uses proteins for essentially everything,” says Grigoryan. “The promise that offers for therapeutic interventions is really immense.”

But drug designers currently have to draw on an ingredient list made up of natural proteins. The goal of protein generation is to extend that list with a nearly infinite pool of computer-designed ones.

Computational techniques for designing proteins are not new. But previous approaches have been slow and not great at designing large proteins or protein complexes—molecular machines made up of multiple proteins coupled together. And such proteins are often crucial for treating diseases.  

The two programs announced today are also not the first use of diffusion models for protein generation. A handful of studies in the last few months from Amini and others have shown that diffusion models are a promising technique, but these were proof-of-concept prototypes. Chroma and RoseTTAFold Diffusion build on this work and are the first full-fledged programs that can produce precise designs for a wide variety of proteins.

Namrata Anand, who co-developed one of the first diffusion models for protein generation in May 2022, thinks the big significance of Chroma and RoseTTAFold Diffusion is that they have taken the technique and supersized it, training on more data and more computers. “It may be fair to say that this is more like DALL-E because of how they’ve scaled things up,” she says.

Diffusion models are neural networks trained to remove “noise”—random perturbations added to data—from their input. Given a random mess of pixels, a diffusion model will try to turn it into a recognizable image.

In Chroma, noise is added by unraveling the amino acid chains that a protein is made from. Given a random clump of these chains, Chroma tries to put them together to form a protein. Guided by specified constraints on what the result should look like, Chroma can generate novel proteins with specific properties.

Baker’s team takes a different approach, though the end results are similar. Its diffusion model starts with an even more scrambled structure. Another key difference is that RoseTTAFold Diffusion uses information about how the pieces of a protein fit together provided by a separate neural network trained to predict protein structure (as DeepMind’s AlphaFold does). This guides the overall generative process. 

Generate Biomedicines and Baker’s team both show off an impressive array of results. They are able to generate proteins with multiple degrees of symmetry, including proteins that are circular, triangular, or hexagonal. To illustrate the versatility of their program, Generate Biomedicines generated proteins shaped like the 26 letters of the Latin alphabet and the numerals 0 to 10. Both teams can also generate pieces of proteins, matching new parts to existing structures.

Most of these demonstrated structures would serve no purpose in practice. But because a protein’s function is determined by its shape, being able to generate different structures on demand is crucial.

Generating strange designs on a computer is one thing. But the goal is to turn these designs into real proteins. To test whether Chroma produced designs that could be made, Generate Biomedicines took the sequences for some of its designs—the amino acid strings that make up the protein—and ran them through another AI program. They found that 55% of them would be predicted to fold into the structure generated by Chroma, which suggests that these are designs for viable proteins.

Baker’s team ran a similar test. But Baker and his colleagues have gone a lot further than Generate Biomedicines in evaluating their model. They have created some of RoseTTAFold Diffusion’s designs in their lab. (Generate Biomedicines says that it is also doing lab tests but is not yet ready to share results.) “This is more than just proof of concept,” says Watson. “We’re actually using this to make really great proteins.”

For Baker, the headline result is the generation of a new protein that attaches to the parathyroid hormone, which controls calcium levels in the blood. “We basically gave the model the hormone and nothing else and told it to make a protein that binds to it,” he says. When they tested the novel protein in the lab, they found that it attached to the hormone more tightly than anything that could have been generated using other computational methods—and more tightly than existing drugs. “It came up with this protein design out of thin air,” says Baker. 

Grigoryan acknowledges that inventing new proteins is just the first step of many. We’re a drug company, he says. “At the end of the day what matters is whether we can make medicines that work or not.” Protein based drugs need to be manufactured in large numbers, then tested in the lab and finally in humans. This can take years. But he thinks that his company and others will find ways to speed up those steps as well.

“The rate of scientific progress comes in fits and starts,” says Baker. “But right now we’re in the middle of what can only be called a technological revolution.”

Correction: A previous version of this article misattributed Joe Watson’s comments.

text:
The story of Harry Belafonte and Petula Clark centers on a landmark, racially-charged moment during Clark's 1968 NBC television special, Petula... 

British singer Petula Clark invited American civil rights activist and singer Harry Belafonte as the sole guest star for her primetime U.S. television special. Near the end of the show, they sang an anti-war duet titled "On the Path of Glory," which Clark had co-written. During an emotional swell in the song, Clark smiled and lightly touched Belafonte’s forearm.

Doyle Lott, the advertising manager for the show's primary sponsor, Plymouth Motors (a division of Chrysler), was present at the taping. He panicked over the brief physical contact between a white woman and a Black man, fearing it would trigger racist backlash and hurt car sales among Southern viewers. Lott demanded they destroy the take and re-film it with the two performers standing far apart.

News of the behind-the-scenes censorship leaked to the press. Public pressure and media scrutiny forced Chrysler to distance itself from Lott, and he was quickly removed from his position. The special aired on April 8, 1968 (just days after the assassination of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.), drew massive ratings, and received widespread critical acclaim. The moment is widely remembered as a groundbreaking milestone—representing one of the first times a white woman and a Black man shared casual, friendly physical contact on American network television.

. . . 

In 1968, a white British singer touched a Black man’s arm on American television. The show’s sponsor demanded that the footage be removed. Petula Clark refused, setting off a controversy that exposed how deeply racial prejudice still influenced American entertainment.

Clark had spent nearly her entire life performing. During World War II, she was a nine-year-old singing for British troops on BBC radio. Before her twelfth birthday, she had made hundreds of appearances, becoming one of Britain’s best-loved child entertainers.

But her greatest success came much later. In 1964, at 32, she recorded “Downtown,” a song that made her an international sensation. It reached number one in America, and Clark became one of the defining female voices of the decade.

By 1968, NBC had offered her a television special of her own. She wanted Harry Belafonte, the celebrated singer and civil rights activist, as her guest.

The two performers rehearsed together for weeks. During their duet of Clark’s anti-war song “On the Path of Glory,” she reached out and rested her hand on Belafonte’s arm.

It was a natural gesture between two colleagues. But a representative of Plymouth, the automobile company sponsoring the program, objected.

The company feared that Southern viewers would react badly to seeing a white woman touch a Black man. The sponsor wanted the moment removed.

Other takes existed in which the singers stood apart. Clark, her husband and executive producer Claude Wolff, and director Steve Binder resisted the demand. The controversial take was preserved, and the alternatives were eliminated.

The dispute became national news before the program aired.

On April 2, 1968, millions of Americans watched Clark and Belafonte perform together, with her hand resting on his arm.

Two days later, Martin Luther King Jr. was assassinated in Memphis.

Clark later recalled being genuinely bewildered by the objection. She had worked with Black musicians throughout her career and had never considered touching a friend’s arm a political act.

Belafonte understood its significance. At a time when television sponsors could dictate what Americans were permitted to see, the performers and production team had refused to let racial prejudice determine the final broadcast.

The gesture lasted only seconds. The argument over whether Americans should be allowed to see it had already made headlines.

text:
ENGLAND: DECODING TUCHEL'S SELECTION 🏴

Thomas Tuchel's starting XI suggests an interesting tactical approach. I suspect he wants a side capable of competing physically and tactically in midfield while retaining enough pace, mobility and attacking quality to exploit Spain's defensive vulnerabilities.

The 4-3-3 provides a relatively balanced starting structure, with Declan Rice, Elliot Anderson and Jude Bellingham forming the midfield.

I particularly like the complementary qualities of this midfield combination.

Rice offers positional discipline, defensive protection and ball-winning ability. Anderson brings energy, mobility, aggression in duels and the capacity to cover significant ground. Bellingham, meanwhile, provides carrying power, creativity, physical presence and the ability to arrive in dangerous areas.

My suspicion is that Tuchel wants Bellingham to operate with sufficient attacking freedom while Rice and Anderson provide the necessary balance behind him.

The inclusion of Anthony Gordon is also understandable. His pace, direct running and willingness to attack spaces behind the defensive line could be particularly useful against a Spain side that will naturally commit players forward when building possession.

Morgan Rogers offers something different on the opposite flank. He can carry the ball through congested areas, operate in the half-spaces and combine with Kane and Bellingham. I suspect Tuchel values his ability to create attacking situations without necessarily relying on traditional winger movement.

Harry Kane remains central to the entire structure. Beyond his finishing, his ability to drop into midfield, link play and release runners into space could be crucial. His movement may also create opportunities for Gordon and Rogers to attack the spaces he vacates.

At the back, Ben White's inclusion ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold is particularly interesting. I suspect Tuchel wants greater defensive reliability and positional discipline against Spain's technical players. Trent offers exceptional passing range and progression, but White provides a different defensive profile.

The Konsa-Quansah partnership also offers mobility and recovery ability. Against Spain's movement and combinations, England will need defenders comfortable defending spaces rather than simply protecting the penalty area.

James Trafford's selection is another notable decision. Tuchel had indicated an intention to rotate his goalkeepers, so this provides an opportunity to assess Trafford in a demanding international environment.

My tactical expectation: England will look to press selectively, disrupt Spain's build-up and attack quickly when possession is recovered. I suspect Tuchel will want his midfield to be aggressive without becoming positionally disorganised.

The bench is also important. Trent Alexander-Arnold can introduce a different passing dimension, Eberechi Eze offers creativity and unpredictability between the lines, while Calvert-Lewin provides a more physical attacking option.

For me, England's biggest challenge will be managing Spain's possession without allowing their midfield and wide players to dictate the rhythm of the game.

If England can disrupt Spain's circulation, win second balls and transition quickly through Bellingham, Gordon and Rogers, they have the attacking personnel to cause serious problems.

Tuchel's selection appears designed to strike a balance between defensive responsibility, midfield intensity and transitional threat. The real test is whether England can execute that balance over the full 90 minutes.

text:
WHEN CULTURE BREAKS NEW GROUND! 🎭

════════════ ❧ ════════════

CULTURAL DEBUTS 🎭

════════════ ❧ ════════════

A CULTURAL TIME CAPSULE ⋆ NOVEMBER 15 EDITION

════════════ ❧ ════════════

🕒 ESTIMATED READING TIME: 15–17 MINUTES

──────────── ◈ ────────────

🎵 Music ⋆ 📺 Television ⋆ 🎬 Film & Animation ⋆ 📚 Publishing & Literature ⋆ 🎭 Theatre ⋆ 📻 Radio ⋆ 🎮 Games & Other Cultural Firsts

──────────── ◈ ────────────

📜 EPIGRAPH

“Every author, as far as he is great and at the same time original, has had the task of creating the taste by which he is to be enjoyed.” — William Wordsworth, 1815.

──────────── ◈ ────────────

🎭 THE CURTAIN RISES. THE CLOCK TURNS BACK. THE MAGIC BEGINS!

"Lord, we know what we are but know not what we may be." — William Shakespeare, Hamlet, Act 4, Scene 5.

November 15 is a date when familiar names stepped into unfamiliar territory—and when new cultural worlds opened before audiences.

Elvis Presley moves from the concert stage to the silver screen. The Bee Gees and a remarkable collection of artists help turn a film soundtrack into a disco landmark, while the Beastie Boys bring rap into a new commercial territory. Television gains a global English-language news voice, Broadway welcomes a musical about acceptance, and a new generation of players meets the Xbox and Halo.

A prehistoric documentary series takes viewers millions of years beyond the dinosaurs. Robert Jordan expands the world of The Wheel of Time, and Michael Jordan joins Bugs Bunny for a leap from a memorable commercial into feature animation.

THE FIRST APPEARANCE IS ONLY THE BEGINNING. LET US OPEN TODAY'S CULTURAL TIME CAPSULE! ✨

──────────── ◈ ────────────

🎵 MUSIC

1977 — Saturday Night Fever: The Original Movie Soundtrack Arrives 🪩

On November 15, 1977, RSO Records released Saturday Night Fever: The Original Movie Soundtrack, a double-album collection that would become one of the defining records of the disco era.

The soundtrack brought together the Bee Gees, Yvonne Elliman, Tavares, Kool & the Gang, KC and the Sunshine Band, the Trammps, MFSB, Walter Murphy, and other performers. Its 17 tracks moved between dance-floor anthems, orchestral arrangements, and slower songs that gave the album a broader emotional range.

The Bee Gees supplied several of the best-known recordings, including “Stayin' Alive,” “How Deep Is Your Love,” “Night Fever,” and “More Than a Woman.” Their falsetto-led sound became inseparable from the film's image of New York nightlife and the era's disco culture.

The album's influence reached far beyond the movie. It became one of the best-selling soundtracks in recording history and helped carry disco from clubs into mainstream popular culture around the world.

🧩 TRIVIA: The original soundtrack contained 17 tracks and included more than the Bee Gees. Tavares performed its version of “More Than a Woman,” while Yvonne Elliman sang “If I Can't Have You.”

🐶 SPOT: The soundtrack album appeared on November 15, a full month before the film's U.S. theatrical release on December 16, 1977. The music was already reaching record buyers before moviegoers entered the disco with Tony Manero.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: A soundtrack can become more than a companion to a film. At its best, it creates a cultural world that continues long after the closing credits.

───────────────

1986 — The Beastie Boys Release Licensed to Ill 🎤

On November 15, 1986, the Beastie Boys released their debut studio album, Licensed to Ill, through Def Jam and Columbia Records.

The New York trio—Michael “Mike D” Diamond, Adam “Ad-Rock” Horovitz, and Adam “MCA” Yauch—combined hip-hop rhythms, irreverent humor, rock guitar samples, and a deliberately unruly performance style. Produced by Rick Rubin and the group, the album brought rap and hard-rock references together in a way that reached far beyond the audience the band had initially cultivated.

Its tracks included “Rhymin & Stealin,” “The New Style,” “Paul Revere,” “Brass Monkey,” “No Sleep Till Brooklyn,” and “(You Gotta) Fight for Your Right (To Party!).” The latter became an enduring party anthem, even as the group's later work revealed a more complicated and inventive musical identity.

Licensed to Ill became the first rap album to reach No. 1 on the Billboard 200. Its commercial success helped demonstrate that hip-hop could command the center of the American album market.

🧩 TRIVIA: The album's 13 tracks included “Paul Revere,” whose reversed drum sound became one of the record's most recognizable production features.

🐶 SPOT: The album's cover was designed to resemble the rear of a commercial passenger jet, complete with the Beastie Boys' name on the aircraft's tail. The visual joke helped give the record the swagger of a rock-and-roll spectacle.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: New genres often break through when artists ignore the boundaries that audiences and industries assume should separate them.

──────────── ◈ ────────────

📺 TELEVISION

2001 — Walking with Beasts Takes Viewers Beyond the Dinosaurs 🦣

On November 15, 2001, BBC One premiered Walking with Beasts, a six-part natural-history series that followed the success of Walking with Dinosaurs.

Produced using computer-generated imagery and live-action techniques, the series reconstructed the world of mammals after the extinction of the dinosaurs. Its opening episode, “New Dawn,” traveled back approximately 49 million years to a planet of dense forests, unusual mammals, and enormous predatory birds.

Narrated by Kenneth Branagh, the program used cinematic storytelling to introduce viewers to creatures and environments that could not be filmed in the ordinary documentary sense. The series included reconstructions of early whales, ancient horses, saber-toothed predators, and other animals that helped shape the age of mammals.

Rather than simply repeat the formula of its predecessor, Walking with Beasts widened the story of prehistoric life. It asked viewers to imagine what happened after the dinosaurs disappeared—and how mammals eventually came to dominate many of Earth's ecosystems.

🧩 TRIVIA: The opening episode was titled “New Dawn” and was broadcast on BBC One at 8:30 p.m. on November 15, 2001.

🐶 SPOT: The series did not present mammals as immediate rulers of a world left empty by dinosaurs. Its opening journey showed that birds were formidable predators in the early age of mammals, a useful reminder that evolution did not follow a simple handover from one dominant group to another.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Good science television makes the distant past feel close enough to explore—and reminds us that the world has been reinvented many times.

───────────────

2006 — Al Jazeera English Begins Broadcasting Worldwide 🌍

On November 15, 2006, Al Jazeera English began broadcasting from Doha, Qatar, launching a 24-hour English-language news service with an international network of reporting centers.

The channel opened at 12:00 GMT and introduced a new global news operation built around broadcast centers in Doha, Kuala Lumpur, London, and Washington, D.C. Its launch expanded the Al Jazeera network beyond its established Arabic-language audience and brought its reporting to viewers across multiple continents.

The first anchors to appear were Shiulie Ghosh and Sami Zeidan. From the beginning, the channel emphasized international reporting, live coverage, interviews, documentaries, and perspectives from regions that often received less attention in established Western news outlets.

Its arrival added a significant new voice to the international television landscape and helped change the geography of English-language television news.

🧩 TRIVIA: At launch, Al Jazeera English was carried by cable and satellite providers reaching more than 80 million households worldwide.

🐶 SPOT: The channel's first broadcast was not simply a studio announcement. Its news teams were already reporting from more than 20 countries, supported by a network of approximately 60 bureaus.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Who tells the story—and where the storyteller stands—can change what the world sees and understands.

──────────── ◈ ────────────

🎬 FILM & ANIMATION

1956 — Elvis Presley Makes His Film Debut in Love Me Tender 🎸

On November 15, 1956, Love Me Tender premiered at the Paramount Theater in New York City, introducing Elvis Presley to movie audiences in his first major screen role.

Directed by Robert D. Webb, the black-and-white Western takes place in the American South during the aftermath of the Civil War. Presley plays Clint Reno, the youngest member of a family whose loyalties and relationships are tested when his older brother returns from the war.

Richard Egan and Debra Paget co-starred, while Presley performed several songs as part of the story. The film marked a major expansion of his public career. By 1956, he had already become a national music sensation, and Hollywood offered another way to reach an audience captivated by his voice and personality.

The film launched a screen career that would include 31 feature films and two theatrically released concert documentaries.

🧩 TRIVIA: Presley received co-star billing alongside Richard Egan and Debra Paget, an unusually prominent position for a performer making his first film appearance.

🐶 SPOT: The film began production under the title The Reno Brothers as a post-Civil War story without songs. After Presley was cast, four songs were added to the screenplay, and the picture was retitled to capitalize on the success of his recording.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: When an artist crosses into a new medium, the result can reshape an entire career—even when the first performance is far from the work that made the artist famous.

───────────────

1996 — Space Jam Brings Michael Jordan and Bugs Bunny Together 🏀

On November 15, 1996, Space Jam opened in U.S. theaters, bringing basketball superstar Michael Jordan into a feature-length live-action and animated adventure with the Looney Tunes.

Directed by Joe Pytka, the film imagines Jordan joining Bugs Bunny and the other Looney Tunes characters for a basketball game against the Monstars, a team of alien creatures who threaten the future of the cartoon world.

The production combined live-action performances, traditional animation, and digital effects. Alongside Jordan, the cast included Wayne Knight, Theresa Randle, and Bill Murray, while a large group of NBA stars appeared as themselves.

Space Jam became a major commercial success and a distinctive piece of 1990s pop culture. Its mixture of professional basketball, classic animation, celebrity appearances, and a hip-hop-influenced soundtrack made it recognizable to audiences far beyond sports fans.

🧩 TRIVIA: The film's original release date in the United States was November 15, 1996, and Warner Bros. distributed the feature.

🐶 SPOT: The idea began with a 1992 Nike commercial pairing Michael Jordan and Bugs Bunny in the “Hare Jordan” campaign. Director Joe Pytka later explained that the advertisement planted the seed for the feature film.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Sometimes a cultural phenomenon begins as a small experiment. A minute-long commercial can become the foundation for an entirely new entertainment world.

──────────── ◈ ────────────

📚 PUBLISHING & LITERATURE

1990 — Robert Jordan Publishes The Great Hunt ⚔️

On November 15, 1990, Tor Books published The Great Hunt, the second novel in Robert Jordan's epic fantasy series The Wheel of Time.

The story continues the journey of Rand al'Thor, Mat Cauthon, and Perrin Aybara as they pursue the stolen Horn of Valere, an artifact connected to the legendary heroes of the past. Meanwhile, Egwene al'Vere and Nynaeve al'Meara begin their training in the White Tower, opening another path into the series' intricate world of politics, prophecy, and magic.

Jordan expanded the scope of the story beyond the foundations laid in The Eye of the World. The second volume deepened the mythology, broadened the cast, and developed the central conflict surrounding the Dragon Reborn.

The novel helped establish the scale and ambition that would define The Wheel of Time, a fantasy saga that eventually grew to fourteen main novels, completed after Jordan's death by Brandon Sanderson using the author's notes.

🧩 TRIVIA: The original U.S. hardcover edition was published by Tor Books and contained 600 pages.

🐶 SPOT: In 2004, the novel was republished for younger readers as two separate volumes, The Hunt Begins and New Threads in the Pattern. A single book had been divided into two parts, giving the same story a different publishing life.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: A successful sequel does more than continue a story. It expands the world until readers feel there is always another door waiting to be opened.

──────────── ◈ ────────────

🎭 THEATRE

2018 — The Prom Opens on Broadway 🌈

On November 15, 2018, The Prom officially opened at the Longacre Theatre, bringing a new musical comedy about acceptance, celebrity, and a high-school dance to Broadway.

The musical follows a student in a small Indiana town who wants to attend prom with her girlfriend. When the school community objects, four self-absorbed Broadway performers arrive, hoping to turn the controversy into a public-relations opportunity. Their plans become complicated as they encounter the young people whose lives are actually at stake.

The production featured a book by Bob Martin and Chad Beguelin, music by Matthew Sklar, and lyrics by Beguelin. Casey Nicholaw directed and choreographed the show, with a cast led by Beth Leavel, Brooks Ashmanskas, Caitlin Kinnunen, and Christopher Sieber.

The Prom blended broad musical comedy with a story about belonging and the right to be accepted. Its Broadway run earned seven Tony Award nominations in 2019, including Best Musical, Best Book of a Musical, and Best Original Score.

🧩 TRIVIA: The Prom had already received its world premiere at Atlanta's Alliance Theatre in 2016, more than two years before its Broadway opening.

🐶 SPOT: One particularly prominent real-life parallel occurred in 2010, when Mississippi student Constance McMillen was prevented from attending her school prom with her girlfriend. The controversy, along with similar incidents involving other students, helped inspire the musical's broader story.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Theatre can entertain while asking audiences to reconsider who gets welcomed into the room—and who has been left waiting outside.

──────────── ◈ ────────────

🎮 GAMES & OTHER CULTURAL FIRSTS

1926 — NBC Begins Its First National Radio Broadcast 📻

On November 15, 1926, the National Broadcasting Company began broadcasting over its newly formed radio network with a gala program from the Waldorf-Astoria Hotel in New York City.

The inaugural broadcast linked 25 stations in 21 cities, carrying a program designed to demonstrate the possibilities of national radio. The event featured performers and personalities including opera singer Mary Garden, humorist Will Rogers, and the comedy team Weber and Fields, alongside orchestras and other musical performers.

NBC's launch represented a major step in the development of network broadcasting. Instead of limiting programs to the reach of a single local station, a network could distribute the same performance and information across a wide geographic area.

The company hoped to increase the quantity and quality of radio programming while making national events and entertainment available to listeners throughout the country.

🧩 TRIVIA: The inaugural program began at 8 p.m. on November 15 and continued until 12:25 a.m. the following morning. Twenty-five stations in 21 cities carried the broadcast.

🐶 SPOT: More than 1,000 guests attended the event in the Waldorf-Astoria's grand ballroom, but the people in the room were only the visible audience. Microphones carried the performances to a much larger unseen public across the country.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: A new medium becomes a cultural force when it connects people who could never fit into the same room.

───────────────

2001 — Microsoft Launches the Xbox 🎮

On November 15, 2001, Microsoft released the Xbox video-game system in North America, entering a console market long dominated by established Japanese competitors.

The launch represented Microsoft's first major move into dedicated home-console hardware. The company presented the Xbox as a powerful entertainment system built around advanced graphics, sound, and a new generation of games.

The launch lineup included Halo: Combat Evolved, Bungie's science-fiction first-person shooter. Players took control of the armored supersoldier Master Chief and explored the mysterious ring-shaped world known as Halo, encountering alien forces and uncovering a much larger conflict.

The Xbox gave Microsoft a foothold in the living room and established the beginning of a console brand that would become a major force in the video-game industry. Halo, meanwhile, became one of the platform's defining franchises.

🧩 TRIVIA: Microsoft announced that the Xbox would arrive in North America on November 15, 2001, with a launch lineup of 15 to 20 games expected to be available during launch week.

🐶 SPOT: The Xbox launch was marked by a midnight retail release. Microsoft reported that customers waited for hours to become among the first buyers, turning the console's arrival into a public event rather than an ordinary product shipment.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: A new platform succeeds when it offers more than technology. It needs experiences that give people a reason to enter a new world.

──────────── ◈ ────────────

📚 SOURCES & FURTHER READING

🎵 MUSIC

Licensed to Ill — Beastie Boys official store, original release date and track listing; AllMusic, release information and historical review; MusicBrainz, U.S. release record.

📺 TELEVISION

🎬 FILM & ANIMATION

📚 PUBLISHING & LITERATURE

🎭 THEATRE

📜 QUOTATIONS

William Shakespeare — “We know what we are, but know not what we may be.” Hamlet, Act 4, Scene 5.

I hear you coach but I’m not sure Mission Viejo falls in that poor us category…..look at the last 30 years of high school football in Oregon and Washington for example and find me an “inner city” school that won the state championship….football has ALWAYS been dominated by money for large classification schools.  There have always been haves and have nots.  

The only time this comes up around here is when kids decide to go to inner city schools that have a little sliver of success for which the coaches are labeled  slick willy “recruiters” despite the fact that they have nothing to offer a family  beyond a sense of genuine care belonging and love and perhaps more concern for what happens to the kids AFTER high school.  

Meanwhile kids and families in these “affluent” areas are in some cases helping families secure jobs, housing, and transportation to win championships for those communities.  Nobody ever complains or draws attention to that  because those communities have the money to get litigious or they just accept that it’s just “supposed” to happen there. 

If you are from the “inner city” you know better because you know how kids who didn’t “grow up and go to school where their parents did” ended up at those suburban schools.  This isn’t a new problem.  The problem is getting more attention now because the “haves” list is shrinking to wealthy private schools and only the most well off suburbs….not just basic suburbs.   People who once benefited more and didn’t really notice are now feeling the same “have nots” issues affect them that have affected other communities for decades.
